title: Cut elimination for equality-free intuitionistic first-order sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)
Constructive Logic: Cut Elimination (Lecture 10, October 5, 2017; edits by Andre Platzer)

summary: Eliminate cuts in equality-free intuitionistic first-order proof trees while preserving their exact contexts, witnesses and protected parameters.
abstract: A proof may use a quantified lemma before applying it to a particular object or an unknown witness. We show how to remove such intermediate cuts from intuitionistic first-order proofs without changing their assumptions or conclusion. Universal lemmas are replaced by the instance actually needed; existential lemmas are used through branches whose temporary witnesses cannot escape. The resulting proofs agree exactly with intuitionistic natural deduction when equality rules are disabled. Their formulas come from actual instances of the end formulas, together with the falsum needed by primitive negation, giving a syntactic proof of consistency.
